 Champions League Champions League: Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal, RB Leipzig 2-3 Manchester City and more – as it happened
 Manchester City edged out Leipzig in a ding-dong contest, while Como ran riot at Lens with a historic 9-1 victory

 7m ago 17.15 EST OK that’s all we have time for in tonight’s clockwatch. It’s been a busy one, frantic in fact, but it’s been an absolute pleasure to watch and bring you all the updates, as always.
 I’ll sign off with a link to our roundup of the other, non-English ties of the evening, with Real Madrid, Borussia Dortmund and, of course, nine-goal Como, among the big winners of the night.
 Take care and thanks again.
 Valverde’s late winner breaks AEK Athens hearts as Real Madrid twice come from behind Read more Share 9m ago 17.13 EST Erling Haaland chats to the broadcasters after his winning goal. 
 “He’s had an amazing start to his City career,” Haaland says when asked about Elliot Anderson, who provided him with a fine assist. “And that’s what you expect to be honest, but he’s been impressive and respect.”
 “I think we need to step up a little bit,” he says on City’s general form. “Keep the ball, work together both offensively and defensively. You can always get better.”
 Share 14m ago 17.09 EST Report: Ed Aarons was there to see Arsenal do the bare minimum to edge beyond Slavia Prague, staying unbeaten in this season’s Champions League , with Viktor Gyökeres stepping up for the Gunners.
 Viktor Gyökeres the difference as Arsenal claim nervy win against Slavia Prague Read more Share 16m ago 17.06 EST Report: Jamie Jackson has been at the RB Arena tonight to witness the inevitable … Erling Haaland scoring a crucial goal to bail Manchester City out of trouble.
 Erling Haaland settles thriller for Manchester City to end RB Leipzig resistance Read more Share 20m ago 17.03 EST Stay tuned for all the various match reports, plus a bit of reaction. The Champions League rarely fails to deliver and tonight has been no exception.
 Share 21m ago 17.01 EST It’s not often a ding-dong 3-2 win for Manchester City against one of the Bundesliga big hitters in the Champions League gets overshadowed, but that Como result ought to attract the attention of headline writers everywhere.
 The other story tonight is a narrow win for Arsenal over Slavia Prague, when many expected Mikel Arteta’s side to run in a few goals. The Gunners boss will argue the three points are all that matter, especially after a tough assignment at Anfield last weekend.
 Share 24m ago 16.58 EST Full time scores
 Borussia Dortmund 2-1 Real Betis
 Lens 1-9 Como
 PSV 1-2 Club Brugge
 Porto 4-1 Napoli
 RB Leipzig 2-3 Manchester City
 Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal
 Viking 4-1 Sabah
 That Como result will grab the headlines, and rightly so,
 Share 26m ago 16.57 EST Como have made history tonight, that’s for sure.
 Share Updated at  16.59 EST 28m ago 16.54 EST Teenager Matteo Papaccioli makes it NINE goals for Como. It’s 9-1 in Lens. Utterly ridiculous.
 And it’s 4-1 to Viking against Sabah after a comedy of defensive errors from the team from Azerbaijan.
 View image in fullscreen My word. Photograph: François Lo Presti/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.59 EST 29m ago 16.53 EST Dortmund are clinging on a tad against Real Betis , but a win would cap a very good week for the Black and Yellows, after they secured a creditable draw away at Bayern Munich in Der Klassiker.
 Dortmund are joint top in the Bundesliga and will move onto nine points in the Champions League group stage if they see this one through.
 Share 31m ago 16.51 EST GOAL! Porto 4-1 Napoli (Aghehowam 90+1)
 Samu Aghehowa slots home a penalty to crown a very good night for Porto, with Spanish defender Rafa Marín sent off for the foul that conceding the spot-kick.
 Porto have their first Champions League win of the campaign and will join Napoli on three points after four games. Will Max Allegri soon be under pressure, given Napoli’s underwhelming start to the season?
 Share 33m ago 16.50 EST GOAL! Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal (Nowak, 90+1)
 David Raya had made a couple of good saves to keep Slavia at bay, but he’s helpless to prevent his one, as Arsenal concede a sloppy goal that stemmed from a long throw in. Wiktor Nowak profits, shooting into an empty net … although VAR are checking it.
 It stands. A nervy finish awaits for the Gunners.
 View image in fullscreen Wiktor Nowak pulls one back for Slavia Prague. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA Share Updated at  16.53 EST 37m ago 16.46 EST Around five minutes still to play in these games. We’ve had so many goals, will we be blessed by even more in added time?
 Share 37m ago 16.45 EST Can Leipzig haul themselves off the proverbial canvas for one last haymaker in the direction of Manchester City? The scoreline tonight is harsh on the Bundesliga outfit, City have been wobbling at times, but the visitors have been clinical when presented with chances.
 I wouldn’t bet against another goal, either way, in this game.
 Share 39m ago 16.43 EST It’s now 3-1 Viking against the 10 men of Sabah – and it’s a good night for Norwegians across the board. Henrik Falchener has netted for Viking, after Haaland and Nusa struck in the Leipzig v City game.
 Como are still 8-1 up against Lens, by the way. They’ve clearly taken their foot off the gas. Poor really.
 Share 40m ago 16.42 EST GOAL! Porto 3-1 Napoli (Kiwior, 80)
 Is that the game signed, sealed and delivered for Porto?
 Napoli have been vulnerable from set-pieces, and it’s ex-Arsenal man Jakub Kiwior who punishes the Italian side here, a good header from Hwang In-Beom’s cross.
 Share 42m ago 16.41 EST Forgive me for stating the obvious, but Elliot Anderson is just a wonderful midfield player you know. Worth every penny of that £116m fee.
 Share 43m ago 16.40 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 2-3 Manchester City (Haaland, 78)
 Superb football from Manchester City, with a flowing move capped by Erling Haaland, who slides in at the back post to convert Elliot Anderson’s fine cross.
 It was an awesome driving run from the England midfielder to set it all up. Haaland, formerly of the Red Bull stable, has hit Leipzig where it hurts.
 View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland sneaks in at the far post to make it 3-2 to Man City. Photograph: George Tewkesbury/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.42 EST 45m ago 16.38 EST Sabah are now down to 10 men against Viking, against whom they trail 2-1, despite taking the lead. A win here would take the Norwegians to four points from four games, which would be a fair effort.
 Share 45m ago 16.37 EST GOAL! Borussia Dortmund 2-1 Real Betis (Karetsas, 72)
 Oh that’s an error from the Betis keeper I’m afraid. Álvaro Valles will feel he should have saved that shot from Dortmund substitute Karetsas – not that the Yellow Wall will care as BVB celebrate restoring their lead.
 Can they hold onto it? Betis were good value for the draw, and I’d expect them to come again.
 Share 47m ago 16.35 EST I feel like the Como nonsense is distracting from the serious business of the other games, many of which are still on a knife-edge going into the final stages.
 Leipzig and City are locked at 2-2, and that’s one to really keep an eye on.
 Share 49m ago 16.34 EST Como have scored an eighth goal, would you believe. Baturina joins the fun. This is getting ridiculously out of hand, actually. Lens 1-8 (EIGHT) Como.
 View image in fullscreen Lens were back in it briefly when they made it 7-1, but the eighth Como goal has finally put the game to bed. Photograph: François Lo Presti/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.36 EST 50m ago 16.33 EST GOAL! Porto 2-1 Napoli (Veiga, 73)
 Gabri Veiga scores for Porto. Could the Portuguese side be heading for their first win of the group stage? That one means a heck of a lot.
 Share 51m ago 16.32 EST GOAL! Borussia Dortmund 1-1 Real Betis (Ruibal, 67)
 A big goal for Betis in the Westfalenstadion! Aitor Ruibal hasn’t been on the pitch for very long but he’s levelled things up for the Spanish outfit, who continue to impress in the Champions League this season.
 Share 52m ago 16.31 EST That Lens goal v Como: 
 (For Oscar, see Ruben Aguilar)
 Share 53m ago 16.30 EST Lens have scored! Sound the alarm! It’s 7-1 now.
 And in the Viking v Sabah game, the Norwegian side have taken the lead to make it 2-1, with Zlatko Tripic scoring the rebound after his initial penalty was saved.
 Share 54m ago 16.28 EST GOAL! PSV 1-2 Club Brugge (Forbs, 65)
 Brugge are back in front against PSV – another team to quickly respond to losing their lead. Carlos Forbs, formerly of Wolves, has got the goal this time.
 View image in fullscreen Carlos Forbs celebrates to put Brugge back in front. Photograph: Bruno Fahy/Belga/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.34 EST 55m ago 16.28 EST Liverpool and Real Madrid’s 8-0 victories over Beşiktaş and Malmö respectively stand as the Champions League’s biggest winning margins. Both records now could be in danger.
 Share 1h ago 16.26 EST 7-0 to Como. Although this one will be checked for offside. Fabregas has taken some big players off but the substitute Mattia Liberali, 19, has scored … and yes it will count. There’s still 27 minutes plus added time remaining in this game. Surely you now head for the exit if you’re a Lens fan?
 View image in fullscreen Blimey Photograph: Jean-François Badias/AP Share Updated at  16.30 EST 1h ago 16.25 EST Antonio Nusa is some footballer, by the way. If you’re looking for your next major import to the Premier League from the Leipzig talent factory – a la Benjamin Sesko, Josko Gvardiol, Dominik Szoboszlai, Christopher Nkunku et al – the Norwegian winger is a very solid bet.
 Share 1h ago 16.23 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 2-2 Manchester City (Nusa, 61)
 What a game this is! City’s lead does not last long this time as Leipzig work it to Antonio Nusa on the left side of the box, and he does not disappoint with a low left-footed finish.
 Enzo Maresca’s side look suddenly porous at the back and Leipzig have what they deserve … again.
 View image in fullscreen Antonio Nusa equalises for Leipzig! Photograph: Maja Hitij/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.25 EST 1h ago 16.20 EST 6-0 to Como. I can’t keep up. Douvikas completes his hat-trick, and takes his UCL season’s tally to six in the process. This could be a cricket score. It’s already a tennis score.
 Share 1h ago 16.19 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 1-2 Manchester City (Fernández, 58)
 City have restored their lead in no time! Ndiaye teases home a superb cross that was begging to be met … and Enzo Fernández is the man! He powers home a clinical headed finish.
 View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernandez restores the Man City lead. Photograph: George Tewkesbury/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.23 EST 1h ago 16.18 EST Honestly, Como are making a mockery of this competition – or maybe just of Lens. It’s now 5-0 to Fabregas’s fantastic team, Marc-Oliver Kempf getting in on the act. A classic case of getting in on the act, actually.
 Share 1h ago 16.17 EST GOAL! PSV 1-1 Club Brugge (Sano, 54)
 This has been another really enjoyable game, from the bits I’ve seen, and PSV have found a fortunate equaliser via Japanese international midfielder Kodai Sano. He squeezed home after an almighty deflection.
 Share 1h ago 16.14 EST GOAL! Borussia Dortmund 1-0 Real Betis (Silva, 49)
 After a watchable but goalless first half, the breakthrough at Signal Iduna Park arrives for the home side, with Fabio Silva scoring a poacher’s goal after Jobe Bellingham’s shot was blocked in the box.
 Real Betis’s perfect Champions League record this season is now at serious risk. As it stands, only PSG and Real Madrid will have four wins under their belts.
 View image in fullscreen Wolves legend Fabio Silva puts Dortmund in front against Betis. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP Share Updated at  16.21 EST 1h ago 16.13 EST This is probably a case of speaking way too soon , but it’s been refreshing not to see too many fastidious VAR checks for handball or other types of dubious penalty shout. The early rounds of this Champions League group stage were riddled with such occurrences.
 Share 1h ago 16.11 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 1-1 Manchester City (Baku, 49)
 That was coming! Another rapid Leipzig breaks sees the white shirts flood forward and this time Donnarumma is at fault. Somehow he’s let a cross from Ridle Baku in at the near post … talk about from hero to zero!
 He should have done a lot better with that, it was simple fare for elite goalkeepers, usually gobbled up.
 Share 1h ago 16.10 EST It’s an absolute procession for Como in Lens as Da Cunha drills home from Nico Paz’s pass to make it 4-0. This Italian team have come to play in this season’s Champions League . Lens are done.
 Share 1h ago 16.08 EST What a save from Donnarumma to deny Christoph Baumgartner. That shot was bound for the top right corner before the Italian sprung high and got an important fingertip to it.
 Leipzig are growing a little frustrated that their attacking efforts have had no reward thus far.
 Share 1h ago 16.06 EST Manchester City are lucky to be ahead in Leipzig, and you sense they will have to step up in the second half to avoid another winless 90 minutes. They cannot seem to get Erling Haaland in the game, chances for any of their forwards in fact have been scant.
 Arsenal’s opponents are more lightweight than Leipzig, but still the Gunners’ sharpness going forward has been notable, despite Mikel Arteta resting the likes of Kai Havertz, Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis so far.
 The second halves are mostly under way around Europe. Let’s get into the updates again. 
 Share 1h ago 16.01 EST Here are the reports from the earlier games.
 Muriqi caps Fenerbahce comeback to make Liverpool pay for defensive lapses Read more Valverde’s late winner breaks AEK Athens hearts as Real Madrid twice come from behind Read more Share 2h ago 15.51 EST Half-time scores
 Borussia Dortmund 0-0 Real Betis
 Lens 0-3 Como
 PSV 0-1 Club Brugge
 Porto 1-1 Napoli
 RB Leipzig 0-1 Manchester City
 Slavia Prague 0-2 Arsenal
 Viking 1-1 Sabah
 And right there, after a hectic 45 minutes typing, I shall take the shortest of breaks! Plenty more fun to be had in the second halves.
 Share Updated at  15.51 EST 2h ago 15.48 EST The half-time whistles are starting to sound. We’ll round up all the scores soon.
 Share 2h ago 15.46 EST GOAL! Porto 1-1 Napoli (McTominay, 43)
 Napoli had wasted a couple of chances to get level in Porto but Scott McTominay – who else? – has found an equaliser a few minutes before half-time. A great reactive rebound effort from the former Manchester United man.
 View image in fullscreen Scott McTominay levels for Napoli on the stroke of half-time. Photograph: Patrícia de Melo Moreira/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.53 EST 2h ago 15.45 EST Paz paid tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel with a t-shirt showing the player’s image, after scoring his goal. Paz grew up on Tenerife and was part of the club’s academy for two years as a boy.
 Share 2h ago 15.43 EST 3-0 to Como in Lens. Nico Paz. Cesc Fabregas is clearly the greatest football coach to have ever graced our good game.
 Share 2h ago 15.43 EST GOAL! RB Leipzig 0-1 Manchester City (Lukeba OG, 37)
 City haven’t been at their scintillating best against Leipzig so far, but they’ve been handed the lead by an awful own goal by Castello Lukeba. There were a million things he could have done with Nico O’Reilly’s cutback … other than to bundle it into his own net.
 View image in fullscreen Castello Lukeba scores a fantastic own goal for Man City. Photograph: Annegret Hilse/Reuters Share Updated at  15.46 EST 2h ago 15.41 EST GOAL! Slavia Prague 0-2 Arsenal (Gyökeres, 38)
 Just when I thought I may be wrong about Arsenal in my earlier post , with the Slavia defence seemingly holding up well, Viktor Gyökeres slides one into the far corner after nice interplay with Mikel Merino. Two-nil and it will probably be more before long.
 View image in fullscreen A superb finish from Viktor Gyökeres to make it 2-0 to Arsenal. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock Share Updated at  15.44 EST 2h ago 15.37 EST Douvikas is now out on his own as the top-scorer in this season’s Champions League so far, with five goals.
 Tresoldi of Club Brugge is there on four alongside a tranche of star names, including Ballon D’Or’s Harry Kane, Erling Haaland, Dortmund hitman Guirassy and Roma’s Donyell Malen.
 We’ll keep tabs on that.
 Share 2h ago 15.35 EST Como have doubled their lead at Lens! Douvikas nets his second of the evening for Cesc Fabregas’s side, who are seriously enjoying life in the Champions League , aren’t they? (0-2)
 Share 2h ago 15.32 EST This isn’t Champions League-related, but a quick check of how West Ham are faring in their first game after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo and appointing Scott Parker … and they are 3-0 down at Cardiff City.
 Jack Moylan has bagged a hat-trick for the Bluebirds. Perhaps there will be no quick fix for the Hammers.
